Let me check the script against what the project memory says.

8:    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
10:    bucket = os.environ.get("EXPORT_BUCKET", "ledgerline-exports-dev")
11:    print(f"exporting {args.env} to {bucket} (dry_run={args.dry_run})")

Yes, but only with `--dry-run`.

A project memory warns that in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the **production** bucket. That's left over from the 2025 migration. A real run against staging would overwrite the real prod invoice reports.

The script has a `--dry-run` flag (`scripts/export.py:8`). It reads `EXPORT_BUCKET` at line 10 and prints the target bucket and dry-run state at line 11. Without the flag, nothing in the script stops it from using that bucket.

Something like this should be safe:

```
python scripts/export.py <env> --dry-run
```

I haven't run it. I haven't confirmed that `--dry-run` actually skips the writes, because I only read the lines that mention the flag. Look at the rest of the script before you rely on it. The printed bucket line will also show whether staging really resolves to the prod bucket.

If you need a real, non-dry run in staging, set `EXPORT_BUCKET` to a staging-only bucket first. Don't use the inherited value.
